findings.message: `attachHarness(opts: { adapter?: StreamAdapter; wrapStore?: (store: AttachmentStore) => AttachmentStore } = {})` declares optional properties without the explicit `| undefined` the rule requires. Production code in the same module follows the rule (e.g. `runTurn` opts `suppressEcho?: boolean | undefined`, `attachments?: readonly AttachmentRef[] | undefined` in chat-panel.ts). Test-helper only, so low impact.
`runShell(opts: { attach?: boolean } = {})` declares the optional `attach` property without `| undefined`. Test-helper only.
`pasteEvent(items: Array<{ kind: string; type: string; file?: { type: string; name: string; dataUrl: string } }>)` declares the optional `file` property without `| undefined`. Test-helper only.

`createInMemoryChatSessionStore(deps?: { now?: () => string; genId?: () => string; maxSessions?: number })` (lines 273-275, and the same shape on `MementoStoreDeps` at lines 134/135/141) omits `| undefined` on optional properties, unlike `deriveChatTitle`'s `timeoutMs?: number | undefined` in cli-adapter.ts. Reported as an observation, not a breach: I could not confirm this Story introduced these lines (git blame was not available), and they look like they predate the attachment work.

Promised live test is missing. vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/live-cli.test.ts holds four live tests (terminal sc2 event for claude and codex, claude review-mode approval, claude auto mode) and none builds a request with readDirs or asks about an image and a text file in the attachments directory. The `--add-dir` argv is only checked as a string by the unit test in cli-adapter.test.ts:1342; nothing checks that a real claude reads the attached files.
findings.expectationRef: live claude: with the argv the adapter builds for a request with readDirs, a prompt naming an image and a text file in that directory is answered from their content

findings.message: Present but failing/unverified. I ran the whole plugin suite (`npx tsx --test 'src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts'` in vscode-plugin): 1161 tests, 1150 pass, 2 fail, 5 cancelled, 4 skipped. The 2 failures are the two manifest-catalog tests the plan excepts (794, 795). The 5 cancelled are not excepted: in src/__tests__/activation.test.ts, 'runReachabilityProbe degrades a hung probe to errored within the bounded deadline' ends with 'Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved' and the four tests after it are cancelledByParent, including 'only extension.ts imports vscode…', which reads the extension.ts this Story changed. The same result reproduces running that file alone. activation.ts is not in this Story's changed set, so this is probably older than the Story, but I could not check git history to confirm; the promise 'every test passes apart from the two manifest-catalog tests' does not hold as run.
findings.expectationRef: whole plugin suite: every test passes apart from the two manifest-catalog tests that failed before this Story

findings.message: Grounding caveat, not a gap. The testsReaching edges are hollow for this Story: top-level `test(...)` callbacks are not graph entities, so symbols such as safeName, nextPath, writing, changePending, submitTurn, runTurn, handleMessage, base64Bytes and findAttachment show empty testsReaching although tests do drive them. I did not raise HIGH findings from those empty edges. Instead I checked the test files and ran the suite: all 26 promised unit and integration tests exist under their exact promised names (attachment-store.test.ts ×5, cli-adapter.test.ts ×2, protocol.test.ts, session-file-store.test.ts, render-registry.test.ts, chat-panel.test.ts ×12, chat-shell.test.ts ×3, extension-chat-wiring.test.ts) and all 26 passed in my run. This is by test name and pass state; I did not trace each changed symbol to an assertion.
findings.expectationRef: testsReaching edges for the Story's changed symbols
